{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Array / Ono Collaboration and Licence Agreement (CONFIDENTIAL)

**Prepared for:** Client (Ono, as Customer/Licensee)  
**Prepared by:** In-house counsel  
**Subject:** Playbook review findings and proposed redlines

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have reviewed the Agreement against the playbook. The commercial architecture is broadly favourable to us: the licence grant, IP ownership and licence-back, assignment/change of control, governing law, exclusivity and supply, minimum commitments, MFN, non-solicitation, liquidated damages and renewal all sit at or above our preferred or fallback positions and require no redline. In several places the terms run affirmatively in our favour (perpetual, royalty-free licences on expiry under Section 13.1; liquidated damages payable only by Array under Section 14.3; no minimum purchase or take-or-pay obligation on us), and we do not raise those.

Seven items require action. Two are critical or structural: (i) Array gives **no IP-infringement indemnity** — its Section 16.2 indemnity is confined to Array Territory activities, Array-sponsored Clinical Studies and Article 15 breaches, while Section 15.4 disclaims any non-infringement warranty and our Section 16.1(a) indemnity is broad; and (ii) there is **no post-termination transition assistance or return/deletion of our Data** running against Array, whereas Article XIV imposes extensive wind-down duties on us. In addition, there is **no monetary liability cap anywhere in the Agreement** (Section 16.5 excludes only indirect damages), **no forward-looking performance warranty** (Article 15 is Effective Date representations only), **no insurance covenant** at all, an **unlimited-frequency Array inspection right** over our facilities in Section 4.9(a), a **post-termination non-compete** running to a redacted anniversary rather than 12 months, and our **at-will termination right in Section 13.2 gated** behind redacted periods measured from First Commercial Sale of both Products.

Two of these — the Section 4.9(a) audit right and the absence of any convenience exit during a multi-year term — are identified in the playbook as walk-away territory. Five of the proposed redlines did not clear automated verification and require manual drafting before the markup is issued.

---

## 2. Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note | Redline verification |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | INDEMNIFICATION; RECALLS (§16.2; cf. §15.4, §16.1(a), §16.3) | No limb for third-party IP infringement/misappropriation claims; fails fallback requiring at minimum a licensor IP indemnity. Cure at fallback: one concise IP indemnity limb, usual exclusions, procure/modify/replace/refund ladder, 3x annual fees super-cap. | Repaired |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | PATENT PROSECUTION AND ENFORCEMENT (§11.1; §§2.6, 2.7, 4.6(c), 13.1, 14.2(a)) | Allocation favours us; §13.1 licence conversion independently satisfies the fallback licence-back. Joint IP consent mechanic (§11.1(c)–(d)) and termination assignments (§14.2(a)(iii), (vii)) sit at the fallback and are noted only. | — |
| 3 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | GENERAL PROVISIONS (§18.9; cf. §18.10, §4.5(b)) | Fully mutual with M&A/successor carve-out; Affiliate consent not to be unreasonably withheld (fallback standard). No Array exit on an Ono change of control. | — |
| 4 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | § IX PRODUCT MANUFACTURING AND SUPPLY (§§9.1(a), 9.4(a)–(b), 9.5; cf. §8.2) | No sole-supplier or requirements obligation; supply is our option. §8.2 is a reciprocal, territory- and field-limited non-compete, at or above fallback. | — |
| 5 | High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Compliant | § XIV EFFECT OF TERMINATION (§14.3; cf. §§7.1, 14.5) | Only LD clause runs in our favour. §7.1 is reciprocal late-payment interest; no termination fee or minimum. §14.2(a)(i)/(iii) cost allocation noted, outside this rule. | — |
| 6 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § II GRANT OF LICENSE (§§2.1(a)–(d), 2.2(a); cf. §§13.1–13.5, 18.9) | Meets preferred position; Affiliates covered as of right, contractors permitted, no revocability at Array's discretion. Sublicensee/distributor consent and no-modification limit noted only. | — |
| 7 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | GENERAL PROVISIONS (§18.3; §17.3) | New York law meets preferred position; ICC arbitration seated in New York or Osaka, neither being Array's home jurisdiction. Court access for provisional relief and enforcement preserved. | — |
| 8 | Medium | MFN — MFN obligations burdening Customer | Compliant | § IX PRODUCT MANUFACTURING AND SUPPLY | No MFN binding us; the closest analogues run in our favour. | — |
| 9 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Compliant | § IX PRODUCT MANUFACTURING AND SUPPLY | No minimum, take-or-pay or volume commitment; we hold rights, not obligations. Volume mechanics deferred to future Supply Agreements. | — |
| 10 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant | § VIII CERTAIN COVENANTS | No non-solicit, no-hire or anti-poaching covenant anywhere; matches preferred position. | — |
| 11 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | TERM AND TERMINATION (§13.1; cf. §§13.2, 14.4) | Single self-liquidating term; no auto-renewal, notice window or uplift. Better than preferred for us. | — |
| 12 | Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | **Missing** | § XIV EFFECT OF TERMINATION (§14.2(a); cf. §14.2(a)(iv)) | All transition and return obligations run against us. Insert reciprocal §14.2(a)(x): up to 6 months' assistance at Array's then-current rates, return of our Data in machine-readable format within 30 days, then deletion with written certification. | Repaired |
| 13 | Low | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | **Deviation (walk-away)** | § IV DEVELOPMENT AND REGULATORY ACTIVITIES (§4.9(a); cf. §7.4) | §7.4 is acceptable. §4.9(a) gives Array itself unlimited-frequency facility access on "reasonable advance notice" with no independent auditor, confidentiality undertaking or cost allocation. | **Fail — manual drafting** |
| 14 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Missing** | GENERAL PROVISIONS (Art. 18; cf. Art. 16) | No insurance covenant anywhere; Array's indemnities are unbacked. Below the fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M). Insert §18.15 at preferred limits; Array may evidence equivalent cover under the Quality/Supply Agreements. | Pass |
| 15 | Low | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | **Deviation** | INDEMNIFICATION; RECALLS (§16.5; cf. §17.3(d)) | Mutual indirect-damages exclusion only; no monetary aggregate cap, so direct-damages liability is unlimited. Fails the fallback's mutual 12-month cap and is materially adverse given our Ono Territory indemnity exposure. | **Fail — manual drafting** |
| 16 | Low | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | **Deviation** | § VIII CERTAIN COVENANTS (§8.2) | In-term leg acceptable at fallback (reciprocal, territory- and Commercialization-limited). Post-termination leg runs to a redacted anniversary, uncapped at 12 months, with no internal-development or M&A carve-outs. | **Fail — manual drafting** |
| 17 | Low | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Deviation (walk-away)** | TERM AND TERMINATION (§§13.1–13.2; cf. §§13.3, 13.4, 8.2) | Multi-year term, but our at-will exit is gated on redacted periods from First Commercial Sale of both Products, with a redacted notice period — no convenience right through development and pre-launch. Array-side element already met. | **Fail — manual drafting** |
| 18 | Low | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | **Deviation** | REPRESENTATIONS, WARRANTIES AND COVENANTS (Art. 15; §15.4) | Effective Date representations plus mutual disclaimer only; no forward-looking performance warranty and no repair/replacement/refund remedy. Conformance deferred to unexecuted supply agreements. §15.4 is acceptable as mutual and prefaced "Except as otherwise expressly set forth in this Agreement". | **Fail — manual drafting** |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

Two findings reach walk-away territory under the playbook and should be treated as conditions of signature:

1. **Section 4.9(a) — Array's inspection right over our facilities (AUDIT).** Unlimited frequency, on merely "reasonable advance notice", with no independent auditor, no confidentiality undertaking, no cost allocation and no limit on access. Our minimum landing zone: independent auditor; one inspection per Calendar Year on 30 days' prior written notice; at Array's cost unless an underpayment exceeding 5% is established; confidentiality undertaking; off-site inspection where possible; no direct access to our systems. We retain on-site access otherwise, given the GxP context.
2. **Section 13.2 — absence of any convenience exit for us during the development and pre-launch phase (T4C).** A multi-year term under Section 13.1 with no Customer convenience right is the playbook's walk-away case. Our landing zone: remove the First Commercial Sale gate, 30 days' written notice, and pro-rata refund of prepaid fees.

We would also treat the **missing Array IP-infringement indemnity (item 1)** and the **absence of any liability cap (item 15)** as high-priority asks; both fail the fallback on a material term, and together they leave us with unlimited direct-damages exposure and no recourse for third-party IP claims on the licensed Array Patents and Know-How.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Manual drafting required.** Five proposed redlines did not clear verification and must be drafted and re-verified before the markup issues: AUDIT (§4.9(a)), LOL-CAP (new §16.6), NONCOMPETE (§8.2), T4C (§13.2) and WARRANTY (new §15.5).
2. **Confirm the two repaired redlines** — the Array IP indemnity limb after §16.2 and the reciprocal transition/data-return provision at §14.2(a)(x) — read cleanly against the existing mutual indemnity architecture and the §16.3 procedure, which we have left untouched.
3. **Issue the insurance insert (§18.15)** as drafted, and ask Array whether equivalent coverage is carried under the Quality/Supply Agreements; if so, we can accept certificates in lieu.
4. **Obtain the redacted figures** underpinning items 16 and 17 (the post-termination anniversary in §8.2; the First Commercial Sale periods and notice period in §13.2) and the §7.4 underpayment threshold, so we can confirm whether any of these in fact sit at the fallback.
5. **Flag for the deal team, not as a legal issue:** (a) the future clinical and commercial Supply Agreements must likewise avoid non-cancellable minimums (item 9); and (b) Array's §4.5(b) restrictions lapse on Array's own Change in Control, which is a commercial non-compete point rather than an assignment breach (item 3).
6. **Sequence the negotiation** around the two walk-away items plus the indemnity and liability cap; the remaining compliant items require no discussion and should not be reopened."}
